newsitem.title: UK: NWE FUEL OIL UP ON REFINERS' LOW AVAILS OF PROMPT.
newsitem.headline: NWE FUEL OIL UP ON REFINERS' LOW AVAILS OF PROMPT.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel barges were steady to higher early on Tuesday, with a lack of prompt product from two main Rotterdam refiners forcing buyers to go to independents, traders said.
High sulphur cargoes were also steady, assessed in the $84/$85 fob region but no fresh deals were heard.

High sulphur barges traded early at $95.50 fob ARA, or 50 cents higher than Monday's close, for very prompt material and were done later at $95 for up to 15,000 tonnes of RMG material loading from August 15 onwards.
Some traders said $94.50 was also done once. Later offers for running refinery material were at $96 and for RMG at $95/95.50 a tonne.
"People are trying to push the market higher, there's a lot of bunker enquiries...The highest numbers were paid for very prompt material, of which there is a shortage," one trader said.
A second trader agreed: "There's a lack of prompt product from two refiners, so people are buying RMG material from independents."
Traders said high sulphur cargoes were quiet but said their levels were steady at Monday's $85 fob for non-Russian material.
